comment: Timekeeping policy for the S10+ (beyond2lte). Read by tools/s10plus/a33/nuxel-time.sh (installed as `nuxelctl time`) and by the nuxel-rtc-check timer. Nothing here is applied by itself: the tool reads it, reports what the system actually does, and refuses to claim a PASS it cannot observe.

timesync.comment_mode: auto = use systemd-timesyncd if it is installed AND enabled; otherwise chrony if installed; otherwise report NO_TIMESYNC_BACKEND (never silently pretend NTP is running).

rtc.comment: The S10+ RTC lives in the Samsung PMIC. The exact driver/binding is NOT assumed: the tool enumerates /sys/class/rtc/* and reports the real name so the claim can be checked instead of guessed.

kernel.comment: Both are kernel-side requirements for RTC persistence and are verified from the running kernel, never assumed: CONFIG_RTC_HCTOSYS (set the system clock from the RTC at boot) and CONFIG_RTC_DRV_S5M-family (the PMIC RTC driver). /sys/class/rtc existing is the observable proof that a driver bound.

launcher.comment: The launcher clock is rendered from the bridge's phone-status payload (services/nuxel-bridge/src/api.py -> _get_system_phone_status, field "time", local HH:MM). Comparing that value with the system clock is what makes 'the launcher clock agrees with the system' an observable statement instead of a promise.

journal.comment: journald timestamps must agree with the system clock; a frozen journald after an RTC restore is a real failure mode and is checked directly.

reboot_persistence.comment: Owner-driven: `nuxelctl time mark` before the reboot, `nuxelctl time compare` after it. The verdict is computed from the two real RTC readings and a boot-id change, not from the fact that a reboot happened.

settings_surface.comment: The Settings -> System -> Date & time page. bg-03 owns this contract; briq-06d renders it. Every value is read with one of the commands below - a page may never display a time or a sync state the tool cannot observe.

fields.label: Set time automatically
fields.honest_note: requires a working timesync backend and, in practice, a network (area 4)

fields.label: Set time zone automatically
fields.honest_note: with location disabled this row must be OFF and say why; a timezone is never inferred from an IP or a guess

fields.label: Time zone
fields.read_api: timedatectl list-timezones (entries come only from the installed /usr/share/zoneinfo)
fields.honest_note: the list comes from /usr/share/zoneinfo; an empty list means tzdata is missing - report that, never a hard-coded list

fields.label: 24-hour clock
fields.read_api: the launcher's own display setting (services/nuxel-bridge phone-status 'time' field is local HH:MM)
fields.honest_note: this is a DISPLAY preference; it changes no kernel or RTC state

fields.label: NTP servers
fields.honest_note: an edit is only accepted when the backend is present; otherwise the page shows NO_TIMESYNC_BACKEND

fields.label: Last successful sync
fields.honest_note: reported as UNKNOWN when no backend exists; never replaced by the boot time

clock_permissions.comment: Who may move the clock. The launcher/status bar READS the clock and must never set it.
clock_permissions.set_time_requires: root (or CAP_SYS_TIME) - timedatectl set-time goes through polkit and will prompt
clock_permissions.userspace_services: systemd-timesyncd (or chrony) own step/slew after boot; the display shows their state
clock_permissions.never: an unprivileged app or a PWA may not set the clock; the bridge exposes read-only time fields
clock_permissions.monotonic: CLOCK_MONOTONIC is unaffected by clock steps and is what the button FSM and timeouts use

last_known_time.comment: Preserve a PLAUSIBLE last-known time so a dead RTC cannot silently produce 1970 log timestamps, and never fabricate precision.
last_known_time.written_by: nuxelctl time settings --record-last-known (and the rtc-check timer when the clock is plausible)
last_known_time.plausible_after: 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z (before that the clock is treated as UNSET, not as fact)
last_known_time.uncertainty: recorded as a floor (lower bound): the record keeps the observed epoch and states in the file itself that it is the last time the clock was observed to be plausible - a lower bound, never a measurement of the current time
last_known_time.use: if the RTC reads earlier than this record, report RTC_SUSPECT rather than silently trusting it

suspend_resume.comment: Reported, never assumed. Nothing here enables a suspend state the kernel does not advertise.
suspend_resume.honest_note: if the list holds only 'freeze', suspend-to-RAM is not advertised and must be reported as not-supported-by-this-kernel rather than claimed
suspend_resume.clock_effect: CLOCK_MONOTONIC pauses across suspend; the wall clock must be corrected by the RTC or the timesync backend after resume, and that correction is observable in the journal
suspend_resume.verdict: NEEDS_OWNER_TEST (a resume cannot be triggered without the owner's finger)

tzdata.comment: Timezone data availability is PROBED, never assumed.
tzdata.if_missing: report TZDATA_MISSING: the timezone picker then offers UTC only and says so
tzdata.package: tzdata (verified against the Fedora 43 ARM64 package manifest in docs/beta-finalization/system/DEPENDENCY-REPORT.md)
